hints.title: Two Dynamic States
hints.text: Maintain two running values: max subarray sum ending at current index without any squared element, and with one squared element.

hints.title: State Transitions
hints.text: No-op state follows standard Kadane. One-op state takes max of starting fresh with x^2, squaring x after no-op, or adding x to previous one-op.

hints.title: Track Global Maximum
hints.text: Because squaring any element produces a non-negative contribution, update global maximum using the one-op state at each step.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxSumAfterOperation(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        dp0 = 0
        dp1 = 0
        ans = float('-inf')
        for x in nums:
            sq = x * x
            dp1 = max(sq, dp0 + sq, dp1 + x)
            dp0 = max(x, dp0 + x)
            ans = max(ans, dp1)
        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every position to square followed by Kadane takes O(n^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two running state variables track transitions in linear O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate extends Kadane algorithm to maintain with-operation and without-operation states.
